problem: The justification says the CPU cannot push about 373 MB per second. That rate (373 MB/s) is well inside what a phone CPU and memory bus can move, so the sentence is technically wrong and a student may repeat it as a hard limit.
fix: Say instead: moving the bytes is not the problem; colouring about 2 million pixels 60 times a second one after another keeps the CPU busy and drains the battery. A GPU does that pixel work in parallel on many small cores with its own memory path, at lower power.

problem: The caption says maps 'start from measured data', but Section 3 describes a metro map as authored vector data (lines, stations, labels), not measured data. This contradicts the text and can confuse the model-versus-measurement distinction.
fix: Word it as: medicine starts from measured scan data, and GIS layers often come from surveys, but in both cases a model is built and then rendered; a metro map is drawn straight from stored vector data.

problem: 'Many small cores that colour vertices and fragments' is imprecise. The vertex stage computes positions and attributes; only the fragment (pixel) stage produces colours.
fix: Write: 'many small cores that process vertices and fragments in parallel, and colour the fragments.'

problem: Segmenting the scan is image processing (finding the tumour region in the captured data), not modelling. Listing it under 'Modelling' blurs the graphics versus image processing line the chapter sets up.
fix: Say: 'Image processing: segment the scan to find the tumour. Modelling: build surfaces or a volume from the segmented data. Rendering: compute a 3D view with lights and cut planes from a chosen camera. Display: show the frames as the surgeon rotates the view.'
